claims.text: Elevated-temperature degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is governed by the gas atmosphere.
Oxidizing environments promote thick, non-adherent oxide scales in the specified alloy.
Non-adherent oxide scales induce microcrack networks at the oxide/matrix interface.
Reducing environments facilitate internal void formation in the specified alloy.
Reducing environments cause localized dealloying in the specified alloy.
Internal void formation and localized dealloying undermine mechanical cohesion and can trigger catastrophic failure.
The as-built alloy has typical additive-manufacturing-induced microstructural heterogeneity.
The specified as-built alloy has a predominant fcc matrix.
The proposed controlled intervention is to compare 5%, 10%, and 20% O2 atmospheres with a reducing atmosphere such as 5% H2 in inert gas at constant total pressure.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from 700 to 900 °C for exposure durations of 50 to 200 hours.
In situ high-temperature XRD can track phase evolution and oxide formation during high-temperature environmental exposure.
Surface-scale composition, compactness, adhesion, and growth kinetics govern oxidation durability.
Subsurface void networks mediate local mechanical integrity and stress distribution in the specified alloy.
Increasing oxygen partial pressure accelerates the nucleation and growth of thick, porous, or non-adherent oxide scales.
Porous or non-adherent scales can spall or crack and create stress concentrations at the metal/oxide interface.
Reducing conditions limit oxide formation.
Reducing conditions promote vacancy accumulation and nanoscale void formation, especially at grain boundaries and interfaces.
High-oxygen exposure will produce thicker, less-adherent scales and associated interfacial microcracks relative to the starting state.
Reducing exposure will increase internal-void density and localized dealloying relative to the starting state.
The proposed oxide-scale or void-network differences should correlate with earlier catastrophic failure.

contradictions.description: The proposed 'high-oxygen' treatments contain 5–20% O2, whereas the stated standard-atmosphere baseline is approximately 21% O2. Thus these treatments are not higher in oxygen than that baseline, making the directional comparison ambiguous.

Catastrophic failure is attributed partly to combined thermal and mechanical loading, but the experimental design specifies environmental exposure without a defined mechanical load or a direct failure-onset measurement.
